newsitem.title: UK: British police investigate ex-minister for perjury.
newsitem.headline: British police investigate ex-minister for perjury.

text.p: British police are investigating whether disgraced former cabinet minister Jonathan Aitken committed perjury when he tried to sue a newspaper and a television company for libel, media reports said on Monday.
Scotland Yard police headquarters said it never names people it is investigating, but confirmed it had begun an inquiry into a case of suspected perjury and perversion of the course of justice.

Aitken last week dropped his libel action against the Guardian newspaper and Granada Television after defence lawyers said they had uncovered new evidence which cast doubt on the former minister's case.

The 54-year-old sued over allegations made in 1995 that he was financially dependent upon wealthy Saudi business associates, procured prostitutes for them and tried to arrange arms sales to Iraq at the height of the Iran-Iraq war.
He also denied allowing a Saudi associate to pay for a stay at the luxurious Ritz hotel in Paris and later lying to civil servants about the affair.

Aitken said his reputation had been "butchered" by the allegations and resigned from his government post to fight them in court, saying he would use the "sword of truth" and the "shield of fair play".
He announced last Thursday that he and his wife Lolicia, who had been due to give evidence on his behalf in court, had separated. She had attended the court with him each day of the 12-day trial.

During the case, Aitken denied lying but at various points admitted a "lack of candour", confessed to "dissembling" and said a letter he sent to a senior civil servant about the affair had been subject to "sharp editing".
His lawyers gave no reason for dropping the action.
